Date of Discovery: approximately 2 months before removal (discovered shortly before removal)
Method of Attack: Contains TurkoRat open-source info-stealer malware that steals account login credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and website cookies
Malware includes anti-sandbox and analysis evasion techniques
Disguised malware as legitimate package dependencies (e.g., axios-proxy)
Typosquatting and social engineering by mimicking legitimate package names (e.g., readme.md file named agent-base, a legitimate package)
Attack Vector: Supply chain attack via malicious npm packages uploaded to public repository
Social engineering through deceptive package naming and dependency injection
Indicators of Compromise: Dependency named axios-proxy imported in nodejs-cookie-proxy-agent
Readme.md file named agent-base in nodejs-encrypt-agent
Approximately 1,200 total downloads (500 for nodejs-encrypt-agent, fewer than 700 for nodejs-cookie-proxy-agent)
Removed from npm repository after disclosure
